messages.subject: Overdispersion with negative binomial
parts:
rstanarm computes a parameter called "overdispersion" when a negative binomial family is fitted.

How is overdispersion defined in terms of negative_binomial_2? My guesses:
  • mu^2/size 
  • 1 + mu/size

In case I missed this in the documentation, please give me a hint.


Dieter

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Overdispersion with negative binomial
parts:
On Tuesday, February 16, 2016 at 2:43:33 AM UTC-5, Dieter Menne wrote:
rstanarm computes a parameter called "overdispersion" when a negative binomial family is fitted.

How is overdispersion defined in terms of negative_binomial_2? My guesses:
  • mu^2/size 
  • 1 + mu/size

In case I missed this in the documentation, please give me a hint.

The negative binomial distribution is confusing. By "overdispersion", we mean what you call "size". In any event, it is the same thing as in the "alternative parameterization" described in help(dnbinom), in section 40.2 of the Stan Users' manual, and theta in MASS::glm.nb.

Ben
